Displacement multipliers converge in L(H^{1/2},H^{-1/2}) with norm <= k. checks.claim: Complexification keeps the same Hilbert operator norm, gives a Hermitian form with diagonal equal to the sum of real and imaginary diagonals, and is compatible with conjugation
checks.reason: Splitting into real and imaginary parts preserves the norm of a real operator. Symmetry cancels the cross terms on the diagonal, so q(u1+iu2)=q(u1)+q(u2). Conjugation invariance follows from uniqueness of the form, resolvent and spectral calculus.

checks.claim: The rough distribution equation gives a graph-continuous embedding D(H_V) into H^{3/2}, with no H^2 or A^{3/4} shortcut; free generator domain H^{3/2} x H^{1/2}

minor: Proposition P:signed-physical-wave writes a bare (2.63) at TeX line 214, without a Teschl attribution at that point. In a section-numbered paper this could be misread as an equation of the notes. A citation form would remove the ambiguity. The mathematics is unaffected.

The spectral-support argument appears only in the next lemma, and the source's explicit forward pointer was not carried over. There is no circularity, because that argument uses only the form bound and (3.52). An explicit pointer would be clearer.

Several symbols are introduced implicitly: the pairing v_V, the object P_V^E (defined only in the proof after appearing in the lemma statement), S_E, and A_{F,m}, H_{m,F} at TeX lines 318-319. Each has a unique reading from parents and the source, namely the F extension of M_m and the F primitive with T. Explicit definitions would help a cold reader.

The conservation probability-one set is built on the retaining extension. P_D is W-measurable, so the event has probability one on the base space too. The TeX does not state this, though the argument is one line.
